Article Title: 3 injured in NIS Patiala ceiling collapse

Article Title: Freedom won by sacrifice, must be preserved by duty: Bhagwat
Article Text:
Hoisting the Tricolour at the RSS headquarters in Nagpur, Bhagwat said Independence Day was both an occasion for celebration and remembrance.

NEW DELHI: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Saturday said the freedom secured through decades of sacrifice carried with it a responsibility to preserve it and ensure that its gains make India prosperous, secure and capable of contributing to the world, as the organisation marked the 80th Independence Day at events in Nagpur.Hoisting the Tricolour at the RSS headquarters in Nagpur, Bhagwat said Independence Day was both an occasion for celebration and remembrance.“Independence Day is a subject of pride and celebration for all of us. If we count from 1857, then continuously for over 90 years, our ancestors attained freedom through various kinds of sacrifices and self-offerings,” he said.Bhagwat said pride in the freedom struggle must be accompanied by a sense of responsibility. “This freedom was attained by us through so much sacrifice and effort; it is our responsibility to preserve that freedom,” he said.Invoking V D Savarkar, Bhagwat said everything “excellent, noble, elevated and supremely sweet” that freedom could deliver must reach the country, and ensuring that was also a national duty. He said India must become prosperous and secure and fulfil its responsibility towards humanity.In Delhi, RSS joint general secretary Krishna Gopal hoisted the national flag at an Independence Day function organised by Shri Keshav Smarak Samiti at Keshav Kunj. The ceremony began with Vande Mataram and the national anthem was sung after the flag hoisting, while a CISF contingent presented a salute to the Tricolour.Krishna Gopal said India’s freedom came after a prolonged struggle and recalled figures from different periods, including Prithviraj Chauhan, Maharana Pratap, Shivaji Maharaj, Lokmanya Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai, Bipin Chandra Pal, K B Hedgewar, Bhagat Singh, Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan and Chandrashekhar Azad.Remembering those who sacrificed their lives or spent years in prison, he said the freedom struggle had continued in different forms across the country.He said India had made rapid progress since Independence and was advancing as a major nation. “The entire nation should unite and move forward, presenting a beautiful ideal before the world,” he said.
Article Summary: Rss chief mohan bhagwat said independence day was both an occasion for celebration and remembrance. “this freedom was attained by us through so much sacrifice and effort; it is our responsibility to preserve that freedom,” he said.

British cyclist Finlay Tarling has died at the age of 19 following a fatal incident during the Volta a Portugal on Friday, Aug. 14. The Welsh rider was competing for the NSN Development Team when he was involved in a collision with a vehicle during Stage 8.The 166.8-kilometre stage ran from Melgaço to Fafe. Tarling was a time trial specialist who joined the NSN Development Team in 2025 and had represented Great Britain in road and track cycling.The incident happened midway through Stage 8, bringing the race to a halt. Finlay Tarling was involved in a collision with a vehicle, although the exact circumstances have not been officially confirmed.Per Sky News, Finlay Tarling was hit by a non-race car that entered the road. Portuguese broadcaster RTP also reported that he was struck by a vehicle travelling in the opposite direction.Cyclingnews reported that a driver unaffiliated with the race had reportedly entered the route, but stressed that the details were yet to be officially confirmed. The Volta a Portugal organisers and Portuguese Cycling Federation later neutralised the stage until Fafe. The scheduled podium ceremony was also cancelled as a mark of respect.“The organisation of the Volta a Portugal and the Portuguese Cycling Federation express their most heartfelt condolences to the family of Finlay Tarling, to his teammates, to the NSN Development Team, and to all his friends and loved ones,” organisers said.Tarling's team also confirmed his death.“We are heartbroken to announce the passing of Finlay Tarling at the Volta a Portugal today,” NSN Development Team said. “Fin was a much-loved member of our team but most importantly, he was a son, a brother, and a friend to so many.”Despite being just 19, Finlay Tarling had already collected several notable results. He won silver in the team pursuit at the 2023 Junior European Track Championships and finished runner-up at the 2023 Junior Chrono des Nations.In 2024, he won team pursuit gold at the British Cycling National Track Championships and claimed three bronze medals at the UCI Junior Track World Championships. He also finished second in the British junior time trial championships.Tarling continued progressing at senior level, finishing second on Stage 6 of the 2026 Tour du Rwanda. His older brother, Josh Tarling, is also a professional cyclist.British Cycling performance director Stephen Park highlighted his potential. “Fin was a talented rider with a fantastic future ahead of him, a loyal teammate and an all-round brilliant young man,” Park said.Tributes quickly followed from across the cycling world. UCI president David Lappartient said Tarling was a young rider with “his whole future ahead of him” and called his death a profound tragedy for his family, teammates and the cycling community.Portuguese President António José Seguro expressed his “deep sorrow” and said Tarling's death had left the peloton, the race and Portugal in mourning. Prime Minister Luís Montenegro also offered condolences to his family, team and fellow riders.Several teams and riders shared condolences online. For NSN, Tarling was more than a cyclist. He was remembered as a son, brother, teammate and friend. His promising career has been tragically cut short at just 19.

Kevin Garnett's fortune traces back to a decision few players had made before him: entering the NBA straight out of high school. Three decades, one championship, and a Hall of Fame induction later, that gamble has grown into a financial empire spanning basketball, business, and real estate.Now, as the Timberwolves prepare to hang his No. 21 from the Target Center rafters, Garnett's journey from a 19-year-old rookie to one of basketball's most recognizable ambassadors is drawing fresh attention to just how far that fortune has come.Garnett's net worth sits at an estimated $120 million, according to Celebrity Net Worth. That figure reflects a career built primarily on NBA salaries, which alone totaled $334.3 million over 21 seasons, supplemented by endorsement income that reportedly reached $10 million annually near the end of his playing days.His earnings didn't stop when he retired in 2016. Garnett has since drawn income from media work, including a run on "Inside the NBA," a supporting role in the 2019 film "Uncut Gems," and consulting positions with the Los Angeles Clippers and Milwaukee Bucks. His stake in Italian soccer club A.S. Roma, acquired in 2011, added a sports-ownership dimension to his portfolio well before his return to Minnesota as team ambassador in December 2025.The foundation was laid in 1995, when the Timberwolves drafted Garnett fifth overall, making him the first player selected straight out of high school since 1975. Two years later, Minnesota locked him up with a six-year, $126 million extension, at the time one of the richest deals in league history.Garnett spent 12 seasons with the Timberwolves before a 2007 trade sent him to Boston on a three-year, $60 million contract. He won an NBA championship in his first season with the Celtics, teaming with Paul Pierce and Ray Allen. His final NBA salary, in 2015-16, was $12 million. Across his career, he earned nine All-NBA selections, 12 All-Defensive Team nods, and 15 All-Star appearances.Garnett's real estate dealings have been a mixed bag financially. He purchased a Pacific Coast Highway property in Los Angeles for $6.4 million in 2003, later pouring millions into renovations that expanded it well beyond its original footprint before pulling it off the market shortly after listing it for $19.9 million in 2018.A Massachusetts estate told a different story. Garnett bought the Concord property in 2007 for $4.625 million and sold it in 2014 for $3.635 million, a loss following repeated price cuts from an initial $4.85 million asking price.The Timberwolves announced Garnett's No. 21 will be retired on Feb. 28, 2027, following a game against the Celtics at Target Center, making him just the second player in franchise history to receive the honor after Malik Sealy."Minnesota is home. That's never changed," Garnett said in the team's announcement, adding that he plans to keep building in the city through his KG Certified brand and other ventures.Timberwolves and Lynx co-chairmen Marc Lore and Alex Rodriguez called Garnett "the embodiment of what it means to compete, to lead and to represent Minnesota," framing the ceremony as recognition of his lasting impact on the franchise.

Article Title: Will Patrick Mahomes play the preseason games? Here's Andy Reid’s latest comments on the star QB's injury
Article Text:
Patrick Mahomes injury update. (Image via Getty Images)

Is Patrick Mahomes playing in the Chiefs' preseason opener against the Rams?

How Is Patrick Mahomes Recovering From His ACL Injury Ahead of Week 1?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Kansas City Chiefs open their preseason Saturday against the Los Angeles Rams at 4:00 PM ET, and for Chiefs Kingdom, it has been a long wait. Patrick Mahomes tore his ACL on December 14, 2025, and spent months grinding through a recovery that most quarterbacks would need a full year to complete. Three weeks of training camp in St. Joseph showed a Mahomes who looked sharp, healthy, and ready. Now, with game week finally here, Andy Reid has made his position clear.Patrick Mahomes will not play Chiefs' first pre-season games against Rams. Andy Reid confirmed it directly: Mahomes will not play Saturday against Los Angeles. "There's a pretty good chance I don't play him," Reid said, adding that the "percentages are leaning that way." He was equally uncertain about the second and third preseason games, admitting, "I don't know if I'll play him in the second or third game."This is not a surprise, and it is not a red flag. Reid has done this before, more than once. After Jamaal Charles tore his ACL in 2015, Reid kept him out of every preseason game the following August, saying Charles needed "a little bit of time." He handled Tamba Hali's knee issues the same way, and in 2023 he kept Travis Kelce out of the preseason opener when Kelce's knee "wasn't feeling right."Reid simply does not take chances with players who matter to him, and no player matters more right now than Mahomes.ESPN's Nate Taylor, who covers the Chiefs beat closely, offered more context on why this decision came together the way it did. He said Mahomes is physically a "full go" at this point, and that if the regular season started this weekend, Mahomes would be on the field. But inside the building, the consensus was firm. Taylor put it plainly: "There's no reason to play him in the preseason. But man, if they played the Broncos on Sunday, he would be out there. " He added that people within the organization believe "the juice is not worth the squeeze," and that while Reid personally wants to see how Mahomes operates in a live game situation, the medical staff's guidance is clear: the longer that knee stays away from contact, the better.Mahomes is not fighting the decision. "I'm for whatever coach says," he told reporters. "I'm going to prepare to play. He hasn't told me anything, so I'll prepare to play and prepare to get myself ready." He added that even without a green light, his focus would not waver. "We'll see where we go from there and if not, I'll be as locked in as I am during the game and try to get myself as ready to go [as possible] for the game."With Mahomes sitting, Justin Fields and rookie Garrett Nussmeier will handle the preseason reps. Fields came in after Gardner Minshew left for Arizona, and Reid made clear he was not brought in for a specialty role. He is the QB2, full stop, with 55 starts of NFL experience behind him. Nussmeier, a third-round pick out of LSU and Senior Bowl MVP, is the longer project. Draft analyst Dane Brugler ranked him third among 2026 quarterback prospects and said his "arm talent and command are foundational traits that generally translate well to the NFL. " Reid summed up the reasoning simply: "We got new people behind him that need some work. The more reps they get, the better."Better than anyone realistically expected. According to Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer, Mahomes has not missed a single first-team rep in training camp, knee brace and all, since the very first day in St. Joseph. For a quarterback who was initially given a nine-month recovery window, that is a remarkable place to be in mid-August.Reid, speaking with Breer, gave a candid account of what that recovery actually looked like. "He's going to do whatever it takes," Reid said. "It wasn't about going back home and going here, going there, traveling, all that. It was about him wanting to be back, ready to play. And so there was a sacrifice there of staying here and knocking it out, working with [Chiefs assistant trainer] Julie [Frymyer] every day and spending seven hours at it, and not always fun, right? But he didn't care.I mean, he was going to do it."Mahomes confirmed the same thing in his own words after a recent practice. "I forget about it sometimes; I try to be smart. It's about learning to play with what I got," he said. "We're just going to keep pushing it so I can hopefully get that ok to go out there and play Week 1."Whether Reid commits to that target is still unclear. Breer noted the coach "didn't want to commit to anything" when pressed on the September 15 opener against Denver. But everything about how Mahomes has moved through this camp suggests the plan is on track.
Article Summary: Patrick mahomes tore his acl on december 14, 2025. Chiefs coach andy reid says there's a "pretty good chance" he won't play. Reid has kept players out of preseason games before. Mahomes is not fighting the decision. "he's going to do whatever it takes," reid said.

Article Title: Why is James Pearce Jr. suspended for 8 games? The incident behind the NFL punishment and how his absence could leave the Falcons’ pass rush in trouble
Article Text:
Why is James Pearce Jr. suspended for 8 games? The incident behind the NFL punishment and how his absence could leave the Falcons’ pass rush in trouble(Getty)

James Pearce Jr.’s February arrest led to the NFL’s 8-game suspension

Why the Falcons’ pass rush now faces a major problem amid James Pearce Jr. suspension ?

The Atlanta Falcons will start the 2026 season without one of their most important pass rushers. On Friday, the NFL suspended James Pearce Jr. for the first eight games after finding that he violated the league’s personal conduct policy. The decision follows a February arrest tied to a domestic dispute involving his ex-girlfriend, WNBA player Rickea Jackson.Pearce can still practice and play in Atlanta’s preseason games before his suspension begins on Sunday, Aug. 30. But the Falcons cannot use him in their first eight regular-season games. He can become eligible for reinstatement on Nov. 2, after Atlanta’s Week 8 game against Tampa Bay.The case started on Feb. 7, 2026, when Doral, Florida, police arrested James Pearce Jr. after an incident involving Jackson. Prosecutors later filed three felony charges on March 13: aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, fleeing and eluding police, and resisting an officer with violence. He also faced a misdemeanor stalking charge. An additional aggravated battery of an officer charge was dropped.The police account said Jackson tried to drive toward the Doral police station when Pearce allegedly followed her and collided with her vehicle.Police also alleged that Pearce drove away while officers tried to detain him and struck an officer with his vehicle. Pearce’s legal team has maintained his innocence.The legal case took a different turn in April. On April 23, Pearce agreed to enter a pretrial intervention program. His attorney Jacob Nunez said in a statement provided to The Associated Press that the state would dismiss the charges if Pearce completed the programme without violations. The agreement did not include an admission of guilt or jail time.The programme later stretched to one year. Pearce must stay away from Jackson and avoid further legal trouble while he completes it. Jackson also dropped her request for a permanent restraining order in May, although Pearce still had to stay away from her during the programme.That legal development did not end the NFL’s review. The league conducted its own investigation under its personal conduct policy, separate from the criminal case. On August 14, the NFL handed Pearce an eight-game suspension. Reuters reported that Pearce had the option to appeal but declined to challenge the ruling.The suspension hurts because James Pearce is not just another defensive player on Atlanta’s roster. He became a major part of the Falcons’ pass rush almost immediately after Atlanta selected him No. 26 overall in the 2025 NFL Draft.As a rookie, Pearce played all 17 games and led Atlanta with 10.5 sacks. He also produced 16 quarterback hits and 45 pressures, setting a Falcons rookie record for pressures. His 10.5 sacks ranked first among rookies in 2025, and Atlanta named him its Defensive Rookie of the Month in January.Now Atlanta has to replace that production for eight games. The problem became even bigger after Jalon Walker suffered a season-ending ACL injury. The Falcons recently signed Cameron Sample to add depth, but losing both Walker and Pearce leaves Atlanta with a much thinner edge group.Christian Harris, JD Bertrand, Samson Ebukam, Kendal Daniels and Bralen Trice now have a bigger role to fill.Pearce can take part in preseason action before August 30, giving Atlanta some time to prepare without him. Still, the real test starts when the games count. The Falcons will have to survive eight regular-season games without the player who led their defense in sacks as a rookie.For Pearce, Nov. 2 now stands as the earliest date he can return. For Atlanta, the challenge starts much sooner.

The nfl suspended pearce for the first eight games after finding that he violated the league’s personal conduct policy. Dennis Schröder is on the move again. The Cleveland Cavaliers sent the veteran guard and cash to the Charlotte Hornets on Friday in exchange for Tre Mann, a straight guard swap that doubles as a cap-clearing move for Cleveland and a backcourt reinforcement for Charlotte. It's Schröder's ninth career trade, and his 12th team since Atlanta drafted him 17th overall in 2013.For the Cavaliers, the deal is about flexibility. For the Hornets, it's about adding a steady hand behind Coby White as the franchise resets around its young core.ESPN's Shams Charania reported the trade Friday, Aug. 14. The move clears roughly $6.8 million off Cleveland's books, pushing the Cavaliers to about $29.7 million below the first tax apron. Mann, meanwhile, becomes a straight salary replacement in Charlotte on an $8 million contract. Because the trade was a clean one-for-one, Mann is immediately eligible to be packaged in a follow-up deal if Cleveland wants to keep shuffling its roster before opening night.League sources indicated Cleveland had shopped both Schröder and Max Strus to free up salary for restricted free agent forward Peyton Watson, who has already turned down a four-year, $70 million offer from Denver.Clearing Schröder's money gets the Cavaliers closer to building a competitive four-year offer of their own.NBA insider Brett Siegel laid out the math on X: "Cleveland is now about $42M below the second apron as well." Siegel added that James Harden's expected return still hinges on price, and that Watson remains the priority target.Charlotte gets a proven ball-handler with ties to the front office. Schröder overlapped with Hornets president Jeff Peterson and head coach Charles Lee during his early years in Atlanta, giving the move a relationship angle on top of the roster fit. He slots in as the backup point guard behind Coby White, with a chance to mentor young pieces like Brandon Miller and Kon Knueppel as the Hornets continue rebuilding around a young core following the LaMelo Ball trade to Minnesota.Once he suits up for Charlotte, Schröder ties Chucky Brown, Jim Jackson, Tony Massenburg, Joe Smith and Garrett Temple for the second-most franchises played for in NBA history, at 12. Only Ish Smith, who played for 13 teams, has more.Trevor Ariza still holds the record for most career trades at 11; Schröder's move to Charlotte is his ninth.Schröder is signed through 2027-28 on a three-year, $44.4 million deal, with $33.2 million guaranteed and a partial $4.4 million guarantee kicking in for the final season. Charlotte opens camp with its backup point guard picture settled; Cleveland now turns to closing out a deal with Watson before the season starts.

NEW DELHI: Sri Lanka's last Test win against India came under Angelo Mathews in 2015 in Galle—the venue for the first Test starting on Saturday. He was a new captain thenWhile all the talk leading up to the series has been around spinners playing the key role, Mathews highlighted that playing rank turners can backfire on home teams."If I am not mistaken, India played on quite a few ranked turners against New Zealand and South Africa. Sometimes, it could backfire. We played on ranked turners against foreign teams and it has backfired for us as well. Because it's not easy as a batsman to play on ranked turners no matter how good you are," Mathews told TOI on Friday.Mathews has been a part of a Sri Lankan team which had heady battles with India, especially on their own turf. He believes a player like Rishabh Pant should be backed by the management as he too could have an impact like Virender Sehwag did in Sri Lanka."I remember when Ajanta Mendis was running through the Indian batting line-up, Sehwag was the one standing tall. He was so destructive and such a disruption. Pant is such a player," Mathews said."Pant takes the game on as soon as he walks into the crease. So, bowlers, watch out. A player like that needs backing. A guy like that who can take the game away within a few hours should be backed," he added.A big part of succeeding in Sri Lanka is to be measured against playing spin.One can't afford to go into his shell. "It's about being proactive. I think if you are sweeping, sweep well. If you are using your feet, use your feet well. So, it's all about using your feet and also knowing your options of how to score runs on those wickets is going to be crucial.Mathews also stressed on the importance of not just focusing on spinners in Sri Lanka. "It's definitely not wise to believe that cricket in Sri Lanka will be dictated only by spin," he said. "I wouldn't rule out the faster bowlers also because they are skillful. Guys like Asif Fernando and Vishwa Fernando have a bigger role to play as well, especially with the new ball," he added.Sri Lankan cricket saw a sharp drop in the number of Test matches they played after the stalwarts like Kumar Sangakkara and Mahela Jayawardene retired. For Mathews, it is a big reason behind Sri Lanka's inconsistent performances."I don't think poor performance or whatever has to do anything with that. It's just that it's disappointing that the so-called big teams or who is not wanting to play too many matches against Sri Lanka is quite disheartening. And I think ICC has a bigger role to play in this," Mathews opined."We have not been consistent throughout which can happen to any team. The more we play, the more we learn. We are playing Test matches one year apart. Sri Lanka Cricket can discuss with ICC and other boards as well and try to accommodate more Test cricket," he added.Watch Sri Lanka vs. India 1st Test Day 1 on August 15, 2026, from 10 AM IST live on Sony Sports Ten 1 SD & HD and Sony LIV.

Article Title: Super Bowl LXI lands on Valentine’s Day for the first time in history creating an unusual football-versus-romance showdown

Super Bowl 2027 brings another major change for NFL fans

Super Bowl LXI is about to create a very unusual sporting dilemma. The NFL ’s championship game is scheduled for February 14, 2027, putting it on Valentine’s Day for the first time in Super Bowl history. With romance and football competing for the same Sunday, fans have already begun joking about dinner reservations, watch parties and the ultimate relationship compromise.The date alone is enough to make the 2027 Super Bowl stand out. The game will take place at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, on February 14, meaning couples will have to decide how they want to spend one of the biggest nights on the American sporting calendar.For football fans, the answer may seem obvious. For couples with different priorities, however, the evening could require some negotiation.Social media has already embraced the idea. One Reddit commenter joked about the pressure on restaurants, writing:"The Valentine's Day brunch reservations are going to be harder to get than a Super Bowl ticket."Another post took the joke even further, imagining the holiday as a test of romantic loyalty:"Super Bowl on Valentine's? Peak relationship apocalypse incoming—guys choosing touchdowns over touchy-feely dates. Ladies, demand a halftime proposal or it's single season next year."The humor works because the conflict is so easy to imagine. A romantic dinner could overlap with pregame coverage. A reservation might clash with kickoff.And anyone hosting a Super Bowl party could suddenly find themselves planning around Valentine's Day expectations.There is also a convenient escape route. The game falls on Presidents' Day weekend, giving many people the chance to turn the occasion into a longer celebration. Couples could celebrate Valentine's Day on Saturday, watch the Super Bowl on Sunday and use Monday to recover from the late night.The unusual date is not the only reason Super Bowl LXI will be significant. ESPN will broadcast the championship game for the first time in network history, with ABC also carrying the event. ESPN has already outlined extensive programming and storytelling designed to build anticipation well before the game itself.The timing also feeds into a broader conversation about the Super Bowl calendar. The NFL has long faced calls to make the Monday after the championship game a national holiday, particularly because fans already tend to treat Presidents' Day weekend as a natural extension of Super Bowl celebrations.Commissioner Roger Goodell has previously discussed how changes to the NFL schedule could eventually push the Super Bowl toward Presidents' Day weekend. In comments cited in the original report, he said:"I think if you went to 18 weeks regular season that would probably occur," Goodell said at the time. "It is possible somewhere in the calendar. Could happen before that just because of the calendar, the way it lays out.But I think 18 weeks would get you to that point, and I think it would be a really great move."For now, February 14, 2027 remains a one-of-a-kind collision between football and romance. The NFL has confirmed the date, and fans have plenty of time to decide whether Super Bowl Sunday will be a date-night disaster, a couples' tradition or simply the perfect excuse to order wings and watch football together.

Brock Lesnar and Ric Flair are two of the biggest names in professional wrestling. But they have had very different experiences in terms of money. Lesnar was a crossover combat-sports star after excelling in amateur wrestling, WWE and the UFC, while Flair made his name over more than four decades in WCW and WWE.But there is a big gap, and public net-worth numbers are best seen as estimates, not audited financial statements. Lesnar’s contracts in the modern era, UFC purses and limited-appearance model allowed him to make individual paydays that were much larger than what was generally available to wrestlers during Flair’s peak years. Meanwhile, Flair continues to earn from his name, appearances, licensing and wrestling-related projects, despite the financial difficulties that have beset his wealth over the years.Brock Lesnar seems to be in a better financial state at the moment. Celebrity Net Worth estimates his net worth at $10 million, whereas NDTV reported an estimate of $17 million in June 2026. Other outlets have published higher numbers, a testament to the uncertainties that come with calculating celebrity net worth.Ric Flair is worth much less. His net worth has been estimated to be $500,000 by Celebrity Net Worth, but other estimates online have put the figure at a much higher number.The variation reflects the absence of publicly verified personal financial records, and the challenge of calculating assets, liabilities, royalties and ongoing income for a longtime entertainer.Lesnar’s wealth is intrinsically tied to his ability to command top dollar. He was an instant star in WWE after debuting in 2002, but he later moved away from the wrestling world to try his hand at the NFL and mixed martial arts before returning to WWE as an established crossover star.Lesnar’s career in WWE has been as much about scarcity as it has been about star power. He was often employed on a limited schedule around major storylines and premium live events for most of his later career instead of working weekly.Lesnar’s UFC career distinguished his money story from most WWE stars. After leaving professional wrestling, he came into MMA and immediately became a big draw. Beating Randy Couture for the heavyweight championship at UFC 91 made him a legit heavyweight champion and gave him a serious bump in commercial appeal.Lesnar has also earned money from endorsements and appearances. Jimmy John’s and other commercial deals are among his previous endorsement deals, and his celebrity status has helped his value outside the ring.He has also kept his lifestyle very private. Recent reports have pointed out that he prefers a rural lifestyle and owning vast amounts of land, rather than the high-profile celebrity lifestyle that many sports stars enjoy.Ric Flair’s financial story started in an era when the economics of professional wrestling were very different. The Nature Boy became one of the defining stars of the National Wrestling Alliance, World Championship Wrestling and WWE, headlining big events and winning championships through a career that spanned several decades.Flair made a ton of money in his time with WCW. One published estimate puts his WCW earnings from 1996-2000 at about $1.95 million. But the size of his earnings did not translate directly into lasting wealth because of taxes, legal obligations, medical expenses and other financial pressures.He also made a lot of money from his WWE career. Flair was a wrestler, manager and personality and stayed a close associate of the company for years. In 2005, during a divorce hearing, it was revealed that his annual WWE salary was reportedly around $500,000, showing how much he could make from wrestling even later in his career.Of the two stars, Flair's financial history is the starkest contrast. Celebrity Net Worth states that in 2000, the IRS filed a lien of more than $870,000 against him, and his further tax problems damaged his finances. The same source reports that in 2019 there was a major medical emergency that resulted in a medical bill of approximately $1.8 million.These pressures help explain why lifetime earnings and current net worth can look so dramatically different. Making millions in a career doesn’t always translate to keeping millions after taxes, debts, medical expenses and other costs.Lesnar’s future financial prospects will probably continue to be linked to his standing as a top-tier combat sports attraction. As his active wrestling career is changing, his name still has value for special appearances, merchandise, licensing and media projects.Flair’s earning model is a unique one. At 77, his money-making opportunities are increasingly linked to his legacy rather than regular ring competition. He still turns up at wrestling events, signs autographs and does other promotional stuff.Lesnar has a path to victory in the modern economics of sports and one of the rare WWE-to-UFC crossover careers. Flair’s financial legacy isn’t so much the wealth he has today, but the incredible value he brought to pro wrestling in terms of sales. Their careers demonstrate two different paths a wrestling superstar can take to earn money: Lesnar with premium modern contracts and crossover sports earnings, and Flair with longevity, character, championships and lasting brand recognition.

Lesnar was a crossover combat-sports star after excelling in amateur wrestling, wwe and the ufc. Flair made his name over more than four decades in wcw and wwe.
